angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G) matched to the same NFL route families, tested against season separation over expected on held-out draft classes; bounded-null story with a Combine-week protocol
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break (turning v^2/r plus braking/driving along the path), z-scored within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and reliability-shrunk; identical code on NFL snaps; rule frozen and hashed in frozen_rule.json
headline_number: Held-out (leave-one-class-out, no-tracking forecast as offset, forecast refit inside every bootstrap resample) slope: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G (90% interval -3.5 to +1.0, n=116); within-class shuffle p=0.38; negative in all 3 classes; upper end = 0.15 catches per 60-target season
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_11/cand_2 (8.28). (1) Plain 45-word lede, SOE defined in plain words at first use, 'should stop'/'wrong way' replaced by 'no evidence of gain; harm not excluded' and 'the data give no reason to pay'. (2) Bootstrap now refits the baseline forecast inside each resample (interval widened from [-3.0, +0.9] to [-3.5, +1.0]); per-class forecast calibration slopes reported (graft from cand_1). (3) Mixed model (player, player x drill random effects, drill x year fixed effects) for reliability: 0.53 for 7 single reps; held-out slope with the mixed-model score -1.3 [-3.9, +1.0]; concrete Combine protocol: second reps of slant, dagger, comeback -> 0.62 (+0.023 per rep), all doubled -> 0.69. (4) Cut-to-throw timing tested for circularity (SOE without time to throw: 19.7 in; with time-to-throw covariate: 13.4 in) and with a player-clustered family-wise permutation over four in-game splits (time fw p=0.26, no better than entry speed or speed kept) -> dropped to one sentence. (5) Targets-per-route channel: family-wise p 0.038 over three usage outcomes, 0.25 without Puka Nacua; trimmed to two sentences. (6) New physics paragraph and Fig 1: raw vs smoothed trace of Kayshon Boutte's hardest cut split into braking, driving and turning parts (turning 0.46 g vs along-path 0.24 g median; smoothed peak 89% of raw). (7) Fig 4 player cards: curves normalized to each player's drill median, marker for NFL peak reaching drill peak, triangle+colour for beat/short, component bar strip, slot/tight-cushion/man/go context; decision table now Action + cost-of-error (picks moved for at most N catches). Player intervals now include forecast error. (8) Fig 2 chain is 1x3 with identical z axes, 45-degree and ceiling lines, merged within-player panel labelled post hoc with family-wise p. (9) Fig 3 forest only, 18-definition grid as an envelope band, catches axis at the bottom; 18-definition held-out slopes folded into one appendix table (worst case -1.3). Equivalence p-values, reliability arithmetic and hash moved to the appendix. 1,836 words by check.py, 4 figures + 3 tables.
open_risks: Headline is still a bounded null; losses down to -3.5 in are not excluded (two-sided equivalence p 0.101)
Not a blind test: all three classes were seen before the rule was frozen; 2026 is the first true out-of-sample score
Mixed model does not raise reliability (0.53 vs 0.58 by mean-then-shrink) and the player x drill variance is estimated from only 70 repeat pairs, so the protocol gain assumes it is near zero
No-tracking forecast is weakly calibrated out of class (slopes 0.40 / 0.64 / 1.33), so the offset residual is noisy
Decision-card scheme reads (slot, tight cushion, man) come from 40 sampled snaps per player and 4 to 14 graded breaks; 'tight cushion <= 3 yd' is a press proxy, not a press label
Word count 1,836 is above the judge's ~1,500 target, mostly from the appendix
